# Canon: naturalloy

How naturalloy says an Alloy formula in English, and why. It is the canon of the package `@bigmistqke/naturalloy`. It writes its terms and claims in Alloy. naturalloy itself says its statements from them, through the [Alloy plugin](../canon-plugin-alloy/README.md) of the canon checker.

<!-- toc:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
- [`@term verbalizer`](#term-verbalizer) — The verbalizer is the part of naturalloy that says a formula in words, from a table of readings that says each name of the formula.
- [`@term formula`](#term-formula) — A formula is a piece of Alloy that states a claim, and that the verbalizer says in words.
- [`@term quantified-formula`](#term-quantified-formula) — A quantified formula is a formula that declares variables, and the verbalizer names them and says their types.
- [`@term quantifier`](#term-quantifier) — A quantifier is a formula that declares a variable and says something of it, which the verbalizer may say as a noun phrase.
- [`@term fit`](#term-fit) — For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier): quantifier_1 fits a noun phrase exactly when all of these hold: - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier whose reading says the variable twice - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier with no fact for its variable beside another thing - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier that says no variable differs from another and holds a condition - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier whose condition is not about its variable
- [`@term predicate-call`](#term-predicate-call) — A predicate call is a formula that names a predicate and gives its arguments.
- [`@term definition-passage`](#term-definition-passage) — A definition is a predicate with a body that the verbalizer says as what its name means exactly when the body holds.
- [`@term by-kind`](#term-by-kind) — For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage): definition_1 can be said kind by kind exactly when all of these hold: - definition_1 is not a definition with an alternative that does not begin with its kind - definition_1 is not a definition with a run of and beside another alternative of its kind - definition_1 is not a definition with an alternative that says something about another unit
- [`@term linked-formula`](#term-linked-formula) — A linked formula is a formula that has a word whose reading a unit holds, and the statement may link that word.
- [`@term series`](#term-series) — A series is a run of clauses, or a rule of two sides. The verbalizer says it as a sentence, as bullets or on one line.
- [`@term sentenceable`](#term-sentenceable) — For every [list_1](#term-series): list_1 can be put in a sentence exactly when all of these hold: - list_1 has three clauses or fewer - list_1 has only items that are one clause - list_1 has no item that holds a comma or has two clauses or fewer - list_1 fits a line when it is put in a sentence
- [`@term line`](#term-line) — A line is one line of a table of readings, which gives a word of the logic its sentences.
- [`@axiom a-formula-is-said-without-loss`](#axiom-a-formula-is-said-without-loss) — The verbalizer says a formula only in words that translate it without loss, and refuses a formula that it cannot say that way.
  - [`@spec a-formula-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-formula-is-said-in-full) — The verbalizer says every part of a [formula](#term-formula), and leaves none unsaid.
  - [`@spec a-formula-is-said-the-same-way-every-time`](#spec-a-formula-is-said-the-same-way-every-time) — The verbalizer says a formula in the same words every time.
  - [`@spec a-quantifier-is-said-with-the-noun-of-its-type-for-each-variable`](#spec-a-quantifier-is-said-with-the-noun-of-its-type-for-each-variable) — The verbalizer says each variable of a [quantified formula](#term-quantified-formula) once, with the noun of its type.
  - [`@spec a-variable-is-named-after-its-noun-and-its-number`](#spec-a-variable-is-named-after-its-noun-and-its-number) — The verbalizer names each quantified variable after its noun and the number it has among the variables of that noun.
  - [`@spec a-variable-is-named-the-same-however-the-formula-names-it`](#spec-a-variable-is-named-the-same-however-the-formula-names-it) — The verbalizer names the variables the same way, whatever names the formula gives them.
  - [`@spec some-is-said-with-an-article-chosen-by-the-sound-of-the-noun`](#spec-some-is-said-with-an-article-chosen-by-the-sound-of-the-noun) — The verbalizer says `some` of a type with the article "a" or "an" that fits the sound of the noun.
  - [`@spec an-article-the-noun-is-written-with-wins-over-its-sound`](#spec-an-article-the-noun-is-written-with-wins-over-its-sound) — When the noun of a type carries an article, the verbalizer uses that article, whatever the sound of the noun.
  - [`@spec no-over-several-variables-is-said-as-no-combination`](#spec-no-over-several-variables-is-said-as-no-combination) — The verbalizer says `no` over variables of several types as no combination of the variables.
  - [`@spec a-call-of-a-predicate-gives-its-variables-numbers-that-are-free`](#spec-a-call-of-a-predicate-gives-its-variables-numbers-that-are-free) — When a called body quantifies a variable that the call already uses, the verbalizer gives it a number that no variable in use has.
  - [`@spec a-variable-of-a-body-never-takes-the-name-of-an-argument`](#spec-a-variable-of-a-body-never-takes-the-name-of-an-argument) — The verbalizer never gives a variable of a called body the name of an argument of the call.
  - [`@spec the-alternatives-of-a-list-reuse-a-name-and-keep-it-taken-for-what-follows`](#spec-the-alternatives-of-a-list-reuse-a-name-and-keep-it-taken-for-what-follows) — The verbalizer gives the same name to the variable in each alternative of a list, and keeps the name taken for what follows.
  - [`@spec the-statements-of-a-list-each-use-the-same-names`](#spec-the-statements-of-a-list-each-use-the-same-names) — The verbalizer uses the same names in each statement of a list that quantifies a variable of one type.
  - [`@spec conditions-that-hold-together-keep-their-names-apart`](#spec-conditions-that-hold-together-keep-their-names-apart) — The verbalizer gives a different name to the variable of each condition in a list of conditions that hold together.
  - [`@spec a-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-by-its-body`](#spec-a-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-by-its-body) — The verbalizer says a [call](#term-predicate-call) of a predicate with no reading by its body, with each argument in the place it fills.
  - [`@spec a-negated-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-as-untrue`](#spec-a-negated-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-as-untrue) — The verbalizer says a negated call of a predicate with no reading as "it is not the case that", followed by the body.
  - [`@spec the-reading-of-the-table-wins-over-the-body`](#spec-the-reading-of-the-table-wins-over-the-body) — The verbalizer says a call of a predicate that has both a reading and a body with the reading.
  - [`@spec the-checker-reads-the-predicates-a-vocabulary-declares`](#spec-the-checker-reads-the-predicates-a-vocabulary-declares) — The verbalizer reads each predicate that a vocabulary declares: its name, what it takes and its body.
  - [`@spec a-negation-is-said-with-the-negative-reading-of-what-it-negates`](#spec-a-negation-is-said-with-the-negative-reading-of-what-it-negates) — The verbalizer says the negation of a comparison or a call with the negative reading of what it negates.
  - [`@spec a-union-on-the-left-is-spelled-out`](#spec-a-union-on-the-left-is-spelled-out) — The verbalizer says a comparison with a union on its left as one statement for each member of the union.
  - [`@spec a-difference-on-the-right-is-spelled-out`](#spec-a-difference-on-the-right-is-spelled-out) — The verbalizer says a comparison with a difference on its right as: the left side is in the first part and not in the second.
  - [`@spec a-disj-quantifier-is-said-with-its-variables-different`](#spec-a-disj-quantifier-is-said-with-its-variables-different) — The verbalizer says a quantifier with `disj` as the same quantifier with the condition that its variables are different.
  - [`@spec a-difference-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition`](#spec-a-difference-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition) — The verbalizer says a quantifier over `A - B` as a quantifier over `A`, with the condition that the variable is not in `B`. When `B` is a variable, the condition is that the two are different.
  - [`@spec a-set-with-no-noun-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition`](#spec-a-set-with-no-noun-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition) — The verbalizer says a quantifier over a set `S` with no noun over the signature that holds `S`, with the condition that the variable is in `S`.
  - [`@spec membership-in-a-navigation-is-said-with-the-reading-of-its-field`](#spec-membership-in-a-navigation-is-said-with-the-reading-of-its-field) — The verbalizer says `x in y.f` and `y in f.x` with the reading of the field `f`, with `y` in its first slot and `x` in its second.
  - [`@spec no-or-some-of-a-navigation-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-the-type-of-the-field`](#spec-no-or-some-of-a-navigation-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-the-type-of-the-field) — The verbalizer says `no y.f` and `some y.f` as `no` or `some` of the type that the field `f` points at. The reading of the field puts that noun beside `y`.
  - [`@spec a-transpose-in-a-navigation-is-said-as-the-navigation-the-other-way`](#spec-a-transpose-in-a-navigation-is-said-as-the-navigation-the-other-way) — The verbalizer says `y.~f` as `f.y`, and `~f.y` as `y.f`.
  - [`@spec a-pair-in-a-transpose-is-said-the-other-way-round`](#spec-a-pair-in-a-transpose-is-said-the-other-way-round) — The verbalizer says `x->y in ~r` as `y->x in r`.
  - [`@spec some-or-no-of-a-set-of-things-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-its-signature`](#spec-some-or-no-of-a-set-of-things-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-its-signature) — The verbalizer says `some S` and `no S`, for a set `S` whose reading takes a variable, as `some` or `no` of the signature that holds `S`. That signature is the one `S` is declared `in` or `extends`, or `S` itself when it stands on its own.
    - [`@spec a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-once-is-said-with-a-noun-phrase-in-its-place`](#spec-a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-once-is-said-with-a-noun-phrase-in-its-place) — When the reading of `S` says its variable once, the verbalizer puts a noun phrase of the signature in its place: "an edge is being delivered".
    - [`@spec a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-twice-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-twice-is-said-in-full) — When the reading of `S` says its variable more than once, the verbalizer says `some S` and `no S` in full: a quantifier over the signature, with a numbered name.
    - [`@spec a-set-with-no-one-signature-that-holds-it-is-refused`](#spec-a-set-with-no-one-signature-that-holds-it-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `some S` and `no S`, for a set `S` whose reading takes a variable, when the vocabulary declares no one signature that holds `S`, and names `S`.
  - [`@spec a-primed-name-with-no-reading-of-its-own-is-said-at-the-next-moment`](#spec-a-primed-name-with-no-reading-of-its-own-is-said-at-the-next-moment) — The verbalizer says a clause that primes one set or field as "at the next moment" and the clause without the prime. A reading of the primed name wins.
  - [`@spec a-set-where-a-variable-belongs-is-refused`](#spec-a-set-where-a-variable-belongs-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula that puts a set or a field where a reading takes a variable, and names it.
  - [`@spec a-field-of-one-value-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-with-its-reading`](#spec-a-field-of-one-value-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-with-its-reading) — The verbalizer says `x.f = y` and `x.f != y`, for a field `f` that the vocabulary declares `one` or `lone`, with the reading of the field.
  - [`@spec a-field-of-many-values-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-member-by-member`](#spec-a-field-of-many-values-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-member-by-member) — For a field `f` that can hold more than one value, the verbalizer says `x.f = y` member by member. For every member of the type of `f`, it says the reading of `f` "exactly when" the member and `y` are the same. It refuses `x.f != y`.
  - [`@spec two-values-that-are-equal-are-said-member-by-member`](#spec-two-values-that-are-equal-are-said-member-by-member) — The verbalizer says `y.f = z.g` as "for every" member of the type of `f`, the reading of `f` "exactly when" the reading of `g`. When one side is primed, it says that side "at the next moment" and the other "now".
  - [`@spec a-rule-of-two-clauses-is-said-on-one-line`](#spec-a-rule-of-two-clauses-is-said-on-one-line) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 is a rule whose two sides are each one clause, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 on one line, as "when" the first side, the second side.
  - [`@spec a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-only-where-it-starts-with-its-own-words`](#spec-a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-only-where-it-starts-with-its-own-words) — A statement begins with a capital where it begins with its own words, and with the name unchanged where it begins with a name.
  - [`@spec two-variables-are-said-to-be-different-or-the-same`](#spec-two-variables-are-said-to-be-different-or-the-same) — The verbalizer says a comparison of two variables as "different" or "the same".
  - [`@spec eventually-is-said-as-now-or-at-a-later-moment`](#spec-eventually-is-said-as-now-or-at-a-later-moment) — The verbalizer says `eventually` as "now or at a later moment".
  - [`@spec after-is-said-as-at-the-next-moment`](#spec-after-is-said-as-at-the-next-moment) — The verbalizer says `after` as "at the next moment".
  - [`@spec until-is-said-as-at-every-moment-before-the-first-moment-where`](#spec-until-is-said-as-at-every-moment-before-the-first-moment-where) — The verbalizer says `until` as "at every moment before the first moment where" the second side holds, which comes now or later.
  - [`@spec always-is-said-as-now-and-at-every-later-moment`](#spec-always-is-said-as-now-and-at-every-later-moment) — The verbalizer says `always` as "now and at every later moment".
  - [`@spec before-is-said-as-there-is-a-moment-before-and-at-it`](#spec-before-is-said-as-there-is-a-moment-before-and-at-it) — The verbalizer says `before` as `there is a moment before, and at it`.
  - [`@spec once-is-said-as-now-or-at-an-earlier-moment`](#spec-once-is-said-as-now-or-at-an-earlier-moment) — The verbalizer says `once` as "now or at an earlier moment".
  - [`@spec historically-is-said-as-now-and-at-every-earlier-moment`](#spec-historically-is-said-as-now-and-at-every-earlier-moment) — The verbalizer says `historically` as "now and at every earlier moment".
  - [`@spec since-is-said-as-at-every-moment-after-the-last-moment-where`](#spec-since-is-said-as-at-every-moment-after-the-last-moment-where) — The verbalizer says `since` as "at every moment after the last moment where" the second side holds, which came now or earlier.
  - [`@spec releases-is-said-as-up-to-and-including-the-first-moment-where-if-one-comes`](#spec-releases-is-said-as-up-to-and-including-the-first-moment-where-if-one-comes) — The verbalizer says `releases` as "up to and including the first moment where" the first side holds, "if one comes", the second side.
  - [`@spec triggered-is-said-as-back-to-and-including-the-last-moment-where-if-there-was-one`](#spec-triggered-is-said-as-back-to-and-including-the-last-moment-where-if-there-was-one) — The verbalizer says `triggered` as "back to and including the last moment where" the first side held, "if there was one", the second side.
  - [`@spec a-sequence-is-said-as-and-at-the-next-moment`](#spec-a-sequence-is-said-as-and-at-the-next-moment) — The verbalizer says `a ; b` as "a, and at the next moment, b".
  - [`@spec a-name-with-no-reading-is-refused-and-named`](#spec-a-name-with-no-reading-is-refused-and-named) — The verbalizer refuses a formula with a name that has no reading, and names the word.
  - [`@spec a-reading-with-no-negative-form-is-refused-and-named`](#spec-a-reading-with-no-negative-form-is-refused-and-named) — The verbalizer refuses a formula that negates a word whose reading has no negative form, and names the word.
  - [`@spec a-type-with-no-noun-is-refused-and-named`](#spec-a-type-with-no-noun-is-refused-and-named) — The verbalizer refuses a formula that quantifies a type with no noun, and names the type.
  - [`@spec a-reading-that-uses-a-slot-the-formula-does-not-give-is-refused`](#spec-a-reading-that-uses-a-slot-the-formula-does-not-give-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula whose reading of a word uses a place that the formula does not fill, and names the place.
  - [`@spec a-reading-that-leaves-out-a-slot-the-formula-gives-is-refused`](#spec-a-reading-that-leaves-out-a-slot-the-formula-gives-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula whose reading of a word leaves out a place that the formula fills, and names the place.
  - [`@spec a-binary-temporal-operator-inside-a-side-of-another-is-refused`](#spec-a-binary-temporal-operator-inside-a-side-of-another-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `until`, `since`, `releases`, `triggered` or `;` with a side that holds one of them, except a `;` after a `;`.
  - [`@spec a-primed-relation-of-a-variable-signature-is-refused`](#spec-a-primed-relation-of-a-variable-signature-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a prime on a relation `Sig.rel` that has a reading of its own when `Sig` is a `var sig`.
  - [`@spec a-construct-the-words-do-not-cover-is-refused`](#spec-a-construct-the-words-do-not-cover-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula with a construct that the words do not cover, and names the construct.
  - [`@spec a-line-of-readings-that-cannot-be-read-is-refused`](#spec-a-line-of-readings-that-cannot-be-read-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a [line](#term-line) of readings that has neither a noun nor a key, and says that it cannot read the line.
  - [`@spec a-bracket-with-no-partner-is-refused`](#spec-a-bracket-with-no-partner-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a line of readings with a bracket that has no partner, and says so.
  - [`@spec a-predicate-whose-body-cannot-be-said-is-refused-with-advice-to-give-it-a-reading`](#spec-a-predicate-whose-body-cannot-be-said-is-refused-with-advice-to-give-it-a-reading) — The verbalizer refuses a call of a predicate with no reading and a body the words do not cover, and advises a reading.
  - [`@spec a-predicate-defined-in-terms-of-itself-is-refused`](#spec-a-predicate-defined-in-terms-of-itself-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a call of a predicate whose body calls that predicate, and says that it calls itself.
  - [`@spec a-call-with-the-wrong-number-of-arguments-is-refused`](#spec-a-call-with-the-wrong-number-of-arguments-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a call with the wrong number of arguments, and says how many the predicate takes.
  - [`@spec text-that-is-not-a-definition-is-refused`](#spec-text-that-is-not-a-definition-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses text given as a definition that is not one, and says how to write a definition.
  - [`@spec a-parameter-with-no-type-is-refused`](#spec-a-parameter-with-no-type-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a definition with a parameter that has no type, and says so.
  - [`@spec a-definition-whose-body-is-a-rule-is-refused`](#spec-a-definition-whose-body-is-a-rule-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a definition whose body is a rule, and says that no words follow "exactly when".
  - [`@spec a-definition-of-a-word-with-no-reading-is-refused`](#spec-a-definition-of-a-word-with-no-reading-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a definition of a word that has no reading, and names the word.
  - [`@spec a-passage-that-starts-with-pred-is-a-definition`](#spec-a-passage-that-starts-with-pred-is-a-definition) — The verbalizer reads text that starts with the keyword `pred` as a definition.
  - [`@spec a-definition-says-what-it-names-exactly-when-its-body-holds-for-every-parameter`](#spec-a-definition-says-what-it-names-exactly-when-its-body-holds-for-every-parameter) — The verbalizer says a [definition](#term-definition-passage) as "for every" parameter, then the name, "exactly when", and the body.
  - [`@spec a-definition-that-marks-its-variables-disj-is-said-with-them-different`](#spec-a-definition-that-marks-its-variables-disj-is-said-with-them-different) — The verbalizer says a definition that marks its variables `disj` with the condition that they are different. A call of it said by its body gets the same condition.
  - [`@spec a-definition-with-a-body-of-one-clause-is-said-on-one-line`](#spec-a-definition-with-a-body-of-one-clause-is-said-on-one-line) — The verbalizer says a definition whose body is one clause on one line after the "for every".
  - [`@spec a-definition-says-each-parameter-with-the-noun-of-its-type`](#spec-a-definition-says-each-parameter-with-the-noun-of-its-type) — The verbalizer says each parameter of a definition with the noun of its type.
  - [`@spec a-definition-is-said-in-markdown-the-way-a-formula-is`](#spec-a-definition-is-said-in-markdown-the-way-a-formula-is) — In the Markdown layout, the verbalizer says a definition with a blank line between its paragraphs.
  - [`@spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-for-each-kind`](#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-for-each-kind) — For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage): when all of these hold: - definition_1 is a definition whose alternatives each begin with the kind of the subject - definition_1 can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind) then [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as a list with a noun phrase for each kind, such as "a spec that cites no axiom".
  - [`@spec the-alternatives-of-one-kind-are-put-together-with-or`](#spec-the-alternatives-of-one-kind-are-put-together-with-or) — For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage): when definition_1 is a definition with two alternatives for one kind and can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as one noun phrase for that kind, with the alternatives joined by or.
  - [`@spec the-options-of-an-or-inside-a-kind-are-one-coordination`](#spec-the-options-of-an-or-inside-a-kind-are-one-coordination) — For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage): when definition_1 is a definition with an or inside one kind and can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as one run of clauses joined by commas and or.
  - [`@spec a-definition-with-one-kind-is-one-sentence`](#spec-a-definition-with-one-kind-is-one-sentence) — For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage): when definition_1 is a definition whose alternatives are of one kind and can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as one sentence.
  - [`@spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-an-alternative-does-not-begin-with-its-kind`](#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-an-alternative-does-not-begin-with-its-kind) — For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage): when definition_1 is a definition with an alternative that does not begin with its kind, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
  - [`@spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-a-run-of-and-would-read-two-ways`](#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-a-run-of-and-would-read-two-ways) — For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage): when definition_1 is a definition with a run of and beside another alternative of its kind, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
  - [`@spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-an-alternative-is-not-about-its-subject`](#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-an-alternative-is-not-about-its-subject) — For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage): when definition_1 is a definition with an alternative that says something about another unit, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
  - [`@spec a-word-that-names-a-term-links-to-the-unit-that-holds-its-reading-in-markdown`](#spec-a-word-that-names-a-term-links-to-the-unit-that-holds-its-reading-in-markdown) — In the Markdown layout, the verbalizer links a word whose reading a unit holds to that unit.
  - [`@spec a-word-that-names-a-term-is-plain-in-the-text-layout`](#spec-a-word-that-names-a-term-is-plain-in-the-text-layout) — In the text layout, the verbalizer says a word whose reading a unit holds in plain words.
  - [`@spec only-the-first-mention-of-a-term-links`](#spec-only-the-first-mention-of-a-term-links) — In a [linked formula](#term-linked-formula), the verbalizer links only the first mention of a term, in reading order.
  - [`@spec a-word-never-links-to-the-unit-its-sentence-is-in`](#spec-a-word-never-links-to-the-unit-its-sentence-is-in) — The verbalizer never links a word to the unit whose statement it is saying.
  - [`@spec a-reading-that-points-at-a-unit-links-to-it`](#spec-a-reading-that-points-at-a-unit-links-to-it) — The verbalizer links a word whose reading points at a unit to that unit.
  - [`@spec a-link-in-a-table-held-in-another-document-goes-through-its-path`](#spec-a-link-in-a-table-held-in-another-document-goes-through-its-path) — The verbalizer writes a link of a table held in another document, to an anchor of that document, through the path to it.
  - [`@spec the-nouns-of-a-quantifier-link-and-the-article-follows-the-word`](#spec-the-nouns-of-a-quantifier-link-and-the-article-follows-the-word) — The verbalizer links the noun of a quantified type whose reading a unit holds, and chooses the article by the word, not the bracket.
  - [`@spec a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-on-the-word-and-not-on-the-bracket`](#spec-a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-on-the-word-and-not-on-the-bracket) — When a statement begins with a linked word, the verbalizer puts the capital on the first letter of the word, inside the link.
  - [`@spec a-reading-held-by-no-unit-has-plain-words`](#spec-a-reading-held-by-no-unit-has-plain-words) — The verbalizer says a word whose reading no unit holds in plain words, even in the Markdown layout.
  - [`@spec a-variable-said-once-takes-the-place-of-its-quantifier-as-a-noun-phrase`](#spec-a-variable-said-once-takes-the-place-of-its-quantifier-as-a-noun-phrase) — For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier): when quantifier_1 is a quantifier whose variable the sentence says once and [fits](#term-fit) a noun phrase, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says quantifier_1 as a noun phrase in the place of the variable, such as "sits in no unit".
  - [`@spec a-noun-phrase-can-be-the-subject-of-a-sentence`](#spec-a-noun-phrase-can-be-the-subject-of-a-sentence) — For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier): when quantifier_1 is a quantifier whose variable is the subject of the sentence and [fits](#term-fit) a noun phrase, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says quantifier_1 with the noun phrase as the subject, such as "a tag names unit_1".
  - [`@spec what-else-is-true-of-the-variable-is-a-relative-clause`](#spec-what-else-is-true-of-the-variable-is-a-relative-clause) — For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier): when quantifier_1 is a quantifier whose variable has a further condition and [fits](#term-fit) a noun phrase, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says quantifier_1 with a relative clause, such as "a unit that is a spec".
  - [`@spec several-negations-of-a-variable-are-one-negation`](#spec-several-negations-of-a-variable-are-one-negation) — The verbalizer says several negations of a variable as one negation that lists the kinds, when the quantifier fits a noun phrase.
  - [`@spec a-variable-that-must-differ-from-another-of-its-kind-is-said-as-another`](#spec-a-variable-that-must-differ-from-another-of-its-kind-is-said-as-another) — The verbalizer says a variable that must differ from another of its kind as "another" before the noun, when the [quantifier](#term-quantifier) fits a noun phrase.
  - [`@spec variables-of-different-kinds-nest-as-phrases`](#spec-variables-of-different-kinds-nest-as-phrases) — The verbalizer says variables of different kinds as nested phrases, when the quantifier fits a noun phrase.
  - [`@spec a-quantifier-whose-variable-would-be-said-twice-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-quantifier-whose-variable-would-be-said-twice-is-said-in-full) — For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier): when quantifier_1 is a quantifier whose reading says the variable twice, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says quantifier_1 in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
  - [`@spec a-quantifier-with-nothing-to-attach-to-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-quantifier-with-nothing-to-attach-to-is-said-in-full) — For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier): when quantifier_1 is a quantifier with no fact for its variable beside another thing, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says quantifier_1 in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
  - [`@spec no-with-another-is-said-in-full`](#spec-no-with-another-is-said-in-full) — For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier): when quantifier_1 is a quantifier that says no variable differs from another and holds a condition, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says quantifier_1 in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
  - [`@spec a-condition-that-is-not-about-the-variable-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-condition-that-is-not-about-the-variable-is-said-in-full) — For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier): when quantifier_1 is a quantifier whose condition is not about its variable, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says quantifier_1 in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
  - [`@spec three-clauses-or-fewer-are-said-in-a-sentence`](#spec-three-clauses-or-fewer-are-said-in-a-sentence) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 can be put in a [sentence](#term-sentenceable), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 in a sentence.
  - [`@spec a-longer-list-or-a-list-with-a-comma-is-bullets`](#spec-a-longer-list-or-a-list-with-a-comma-is-bullets) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 is a run of clauses joined by and or by or and cannot be put in a [sentence](#term-sentenceable), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 as bullets.
    - [`@spec a-list-of-more-than-three-clauses-is-bullets`](#spec-a-list-of-more-than-three-clauses-is-bullets) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 has more than three clauses, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 as bullets.
    - [`@spec a-list-with-a-comma-in-an-item-and-more-than-two-clauses-is-bullets`](#spec-a-list-with-a-comma-in-an-item-and-more-than-two-clauses-is-bullets) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 has an item that holds a comma and has more than two clauses, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 as bullets.
    - [`@spec a-list-too-long-for-a-line-is-bullets`](#spec-a-list-too-long-for-a-line-is-bullets) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 is longer than a line when it is put in a sentence, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 as bullets.
    - [`@spec an-item-that-is-more-than-a-clause-makes-the-list-bullets`](#spec-an-item-that-is-more-than-a-clause-makes-the-list-bullets) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 has an item that is more than one clause, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 as bullets.
  - [`@spec an-and-inside-an-or-is-kept-apart`](#spec-an-and-inside-an-or-is-kept-apart) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 is a list of alternatives where one alternative holds an and, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 as bullets that cannot be read two ways.
  - [`@spec a-subject-is-said-once-when-clauses-begin-with-it`](#spec-a-subject-is-said-once-when-clauses-begin-with-it) — In a list said as a sentence, the verbalizer says once a subject that its clauses begin with.
  - [`@spec a-pair-of-variables-is-said-as-it-is-and-not-as-a-subject`](#spec-a-pair-of-variables-is-said-as-it-is-and-not-as-a-subject) — In a list said as a sentence, the verbalizer says a clause about a pair of variables as it is, not as a shared subject.
  - [`@spec a-rule-keeps-its-then-before-a-time-phrase`](#spec-a-rule-keeps-its-then-before-a-time-phrase) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 is a rule whose two sides are each one clause and is a rule whose second side begins with a time phrase, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 with "then" before the time phrase.
  - [`@spec a-rule-drops-its-then-before-anything-else`](#spec-a-rule-drops-its-then-before-anything-else) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when all of these hold: - list_1 is a rule whose two sides are each one clause - list_1 is not a rule whose second side begins with a time phrase then [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 without "then".
  - [`@spec a-rule-with-a-list-for-a-side-puts-its-then-on-a-line-of-its-own`](#spec-a-rule-with-a-list-for-a-side-puts-its-then-on-a-line-of-its-own) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 is a rule with a first side and a second and is not a rule whose two sides are each one clause, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 with "then" at the start of the second side, on a line of its own.
<!-- toc:end -->

## Terms

### @term verbalizer

> The verbalizer is the part of naturalloy that says a formula in words, from a table of readings that says each name of the formula.

A reading gives the positive and the negative words for a set, a field, a relation or a predicate. A noun gives the words for a signature.

```alloy bounds
for 6
```

### @term formula

> A formula is a piece of Alloy that states a claim, and that the verbalizer says in words.

```alloy vocabulary
```

```readings
```

### @term quantified-formula

> A quantified formula is a formula that declares variables, and the verbalizer names them and says their types.

```alloy vocabulary
```

```readings
```

### @term quantifier

> A quantifier is a formula that declares a variable and says something of it, which the verbalizer may say as a noun phrase.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Quantifier {}
sig VariableOnce, AsNounPhrase, VariableSubject, AsSubjectPhrase, VariableWithCondition, RelativeClause in Quantifier {}
sig OneNegation, SaysAnother, NestsPhrases in Quantifier {}
sig VariableTwice, NothingToAttach, NoWithAnother, ConditionAside, InFull in Quantifier {}
fact quantifier_wordings { no AsNounPhrase & InFull and AsSubjectPhrase + RelativeClause + OneNegation + SaysAnother + NestsPhrases in AsNounPhrase and no VariableOnce & VariableTwice }
```

```readings
noun Quantifier: [quantifier]
VariableOnce: {1} is a quantifier whose variable the sentence says once | {1} is not a quantifier whose variable the sentence says once
AsNounPhrase: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} as a noun phrase in the place of the variable, such as "sits in no unit" | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} as a noun phrase in the place of the variable, such as "sits in no unit"
VariableSubject: {1} is a quantifier whose variable is the subject of the sentence | {1} is not a quantifier whose variable is the subject of the sentence
AsSubjectPhrase: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} with the noun phrase as the subject, such as "a tag names unit_1" | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} with the noun phrase as the subject, such as "a tag names unit_1"
VariableWithCondition: {1} is a quantifier whose variable has a further condition | {1} is not a quantifier whose variable has a further condition
RelativeClause: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} with a relative clause, such as "a unit that is a spec" | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} with a relative clause, such as "a unit that is a spec"
OneNegation: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} with one negation that lists the kinds | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} with one negation that lists the kinds
SaysAnother: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} with "another" before the noun | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} with "another" before the noun
NestsPhrases: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} as nested phrases, such as "a test checks a bug that sits in unit_1" | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} as nested phrases, such as "a test checks a bug that sits in unit_1"
VariableTwice: {1} is a quantifier whose reading says the variable twice | {1} is not a quantifier whose reading says the variable twice
NothingToAttach: {1} is a quantifier with no fact for its variable beside another thing | {1} is not a quantifier with no fact for its variable beside another thing
NoWithAnother: {1} is a quantifier that says no variable differs from another and holds a condition | {1} is not a quantifier that says no variable differs from another and holds a condition
ConditionAside: {1} is a quantifier whose condition is not about its variable | {1} is not a quantifier whose condition is not about its variable
InFull: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} in full, with "there is" and the numbered name | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} in full, with "there is" and the numbered name
```

### @term fit

<!-- statement-term-fit:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [quantifier_1](#term-quantifier):
>
> quantifier_1 fits a noun phrase exactly when all of these hold:
> - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier whose reading says the variable twice
> - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier with no fact for its variable beside another thing
> - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier that says no variable differs from another and holds a condition
> - quantifier_1 is not a quantifier whose condition is not about its variable
<!-- statement-term-fit:end -->

```alloy
pred fits[f: Quantifier] { f not in VariableTwice and f not in NothingToAttach and f not in NoWithAnother and f not in ConditionAside }
```

```readings
fits: {1} [fits] a noun phrase | {1} does not [fit] a noun phrase
```

### @term definition-passage

> A definition is a predicate with a body that the verbalizer says as what its name means exactly when the body holds.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Definition {}
sig GuardedByKind, PhrasePerKind, SameKindTwice, JoinedWithOr, OrInsideKind, OneCoordination in Definition {}
sig OneKind, OneSentenceKind, NoKindFirst, AmbiguousAnd, NotAboutSubject, AsItStands in Definition {}
fact case_wordings { no PhrasePerKind & AsItStands and JoinedWithOr + OneCoordination + OneSentenceKind in PhrasePerKind and no GuardedByKind & NoKindFirst }
```

```readings
noun Definition: [definition]
GuardedByKind: {1} is a definition whose alternatives each begin with the kind of the subject | {1} is not a definition whose alternatives each begin with the kind of the subject
PhrasePerKind: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} as a list with a noun phrase for each kind, such as "a spec that cites no axiom" | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} as a list with a noun phrase for each kind, such as "a spec that cites no axiom"
SameKindTwice: {1} is a definition with two alternatives for one kind | {1} is not a definition with two alternatives for one kind
JoinedWithOr: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} as one noun phrase for that kind, with the alternatives joined by or | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} as one noun phrase for that kind, with the alternatives joined by or
OrInsideKind: {1} is a definition with an or inside one kind | {1} is not a definition with an or inside one kind
OneCoordination: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} as one run of clauses joined by commas and or | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} as one run of clauses joined by commas and or
OneKind: {1} is a definition whose alternatives are of one kind | {1} is not a definition whose alternatives are of one kind
OneSentenceKind: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} as one sentence | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} as one sentence
NoKindFirst: {1} is a definition with an alternative that does not begin with its kind | {1} is not a definition with an alternative that does not begin with its kind
AmbiguousAnd: {1} is a definition with a run of and beside another alternative of its kind | {1} is not a definition with a run of and beside another alternative of its kind
NotAboutSubject: {1} is a definition with an alternative that says something about another unit | {1} is not a definition with an alternative that says something about another unit
AsItStands: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} as a list of the alternatives as they stand | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} as a list of the alternatives as they stand
```

<!-- statement-scenario-1-term-definition-passage:end -->

### @term by-kind

<!-- statement-term-by-kind:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->

### @term series

> A series is a run of clauses, or a rule of two sides. The verbalizer says it as a sentence, as bullets or on one line.

A list becomes a sentence only if four things hold:

- It has three clauses or fewer.
- Every item is one clause.
- No item holds a comma, unless the list has two clauses.
- The sentence fits a line.

Any other list becomes bullets.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Series {}
sig Items, Rule, Few, Many, MoreThanTwo, NotClause, CommaItem, TooLong, AndInOr in Series {}
sig AsSentence, AsBullets, KeepsAndApart, SharedSubject, PairInList in Series {}
sig OneLineRule, TimeSecond, OneLine, KeepsThen, DropsThen, ThenOwnLine in Series {}
fact series_wordings { no Items & Rule and Items = Few + Many and no Few & Many and Many in MoreThanTwo and AndInOr in NotClause and no AsSentence & AsBullets and KeepsAndApart in AsBullets and (Few + Many + NotClause + CommaItem + TooLong + SharedSubject + PairInList) in Items and (OneLineRule + TimeSecond) in Rule and no KeepsThen & DropsThen and no OneLine & ThenOwnLine and (KeepsThen + DropsThen) in OneLine and ThenOwnLine in Rule }
```

```readings
noun Series: [list]
Items: {1} is a run of clauses joined by and or by or | {1} is not a run of clauses joined by and or by or
Rule: {1} is a rule with a first side and a second | {1} is not a rule with a first side and a second
Few: {1} has three clauses or fewer | {1} has more than three clauses
Many: {1} has more than three clauses | {1} has three clauses or fewer
MoreThanTwo: {1} has more than two clauses | {1} has two clauses or fewer
NotClause: {1} has an item that is more than one clause | {1} has only items that are one clause
CommaItem: {1} has an item that holds a comma | {1} has no item that holds a comma
TooLong: {1} is longer than a line when it is put in a sentence | {1} fits a line when it is put in a sentence
AndInOr: {1} is a list of alternatives where one alternative holds an and | {1} is not a list of alternatives where one alternative holds an and
AsSentence: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} in a sentence | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} in a sentence
AsBullets: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} as bullets | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} as bullets
KeepsAndApart: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} as bullets that cannot be read two ways | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} as bullets that cannot be read two ways
SharedSubject: {1} has clauses that begin with the same subject | {1} has no clauses that begin with the same subject
PairInList: {1} has a clause about a pair of variables | {1} has no clause about a pair of variables
OneLineRule: {1} is a rule whose two sides are each one clause | {1} is not a rule whose two sides are each one clause
TimeSecond: {1} is a rule whose second side begins with a time phrase | {1} is not a rule whose second side begins with a time phrase
OneLine: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} on one line, as "when" the first side, the second side | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} on one line, as "when" the first side, the second side
KeepsThen: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} with "then" before the time phrase | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} with "then" before the time phrase
DropsThen: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} without "then" | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} without "then"
ThenOwnLine: [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says {1} with "then" at the start of the second side, on a line of its own | [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) does not say {1} with "then" at the start of the second side, on a line of its own
```

<!-- statement-scenario-1-term-series:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> It must be possible that:
>
> There is a list_1 such that list_1 has three clauses or fewer, has an item that holds a comma and has more than two clauses.
<!-- statement-scenario-1-term-series:end -->

```alloy scenario
some f: Series | f in Few and f in CommaItem and f in MoreThanTwo
```

<!-- statement-scenario-2-term-series:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> It must be possible that:
>
> There is a list_1 such that list_1 has three clauses or fewer and is longer than a line when it is put in a sentence.
<!-- statement-scenario-2-term-series:end -->

```alloy scenario
some f: Series | f in Few and f in TooLong
```

> It must be possible that:

> There is a list_1 such that list_1 has clauses that begin with the same subject and has more than three clauses.
<!-- statement-scenario-3-term-series:end -->

```alloy scenario
some f: Series | f in SharedSubject and f in Many
```

<!-- statement-scenario-4-term-series:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> It must be possible that:
>
> There is a list_1 such that list_1 has a clause about a pair of variables and has an item that is more than one clause.
<!-- statement-scenario-4-term-series:end -->


> - list_1 is not a rule whose two sides are each one clause

### @term sentenceable

<!-- statement-term-sentenceable:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [list_1](#term-series):
>
> list_1 can be put in a sentence exactly when all of these hold:
> - list_1 has three clauses or fewer
> - list_1 has only items that are one clause
> - list_1 has no item that holds a comma or has two clauses or fewer
> - list_1 fits a line when it is put in a sentence
<!-- statement-term-sentenceable:end -->

```alloy
pred sentenceable[f: Series] { f in Few and f not in NotClause and (f not in CommaItem or f not in MoreThanTwo) and f not in TooLong }
```

```readings
sentenceable: {1} can be put in a [sentence] | {1} cannot be put in a [sentence]
```

### @term line

> A line is one line of a table of readings, which gives a word of the logic its sentences.

```alloy vocabulary
```

```readings
```

## @axiom a-formula-is-said-without-loss

> The verbalizer says a formula only in words that translate it without loss, and refuses a formula that it cannot say that way.

This follows because a reader learns from the words what the formula claims. Words that say more or less than the formula mislead that reader, so a refusal is better than a loss. How natural the words sound comes after.

#### @spec a-formula-is-said-in-full

> The verbalizer says every part of a [formula](#term-formula), and leaves none unsaid.

This follows because a statement that leaves a part of its formula out says less than the logic holds.

#### @spec a-formula-is-said-the-same-way-every-time

> The verbalizer says a formula in the same words every time.

This follows because a reader who sees the statement change between two runs cannot tell whether the logic changed.

#### @spec a-quantifier-is-said-with-the-noun-of-its-type-for-each-variable

> The verbalizer says each variable of a [quantified formula](#term-quantified-formula) once, with the noun of its type.

This follows because the noun tells the reader what kind of thing the variable stands for, and each variable is a thing of its own.

#### @spec a-variable-is-named-after-its-noun-and-its-number

> The verbalizer names each quantified variable after its noun and the number it has among the variables of that noun.

This follows because a name such as unit_1 tells the reader the kind of the variable wherever it shows.

#### @spec a-variable-is-named-the-same-however-the-formula-names-it

> The verbalizer names the variables the same way, whatever names the formula gives them.

This follows because the name the author chose says nothing about the logic, and a statement must not change when the author renames a variable.

#### @spec some-is-said-with-an-article-chosen-by-the-sound-of-the-noun

> The verbalizer says `some` of a type with the article "a" or "an" that fits the sound of the noun.

This follows because English picks the article from the sound of the noun, and a reader notices a wrong one.

#### @spec an-article-the-noun-is-written-with-wins-over-its-sound

> When the noun of a type carries an article, the verbalizer uses that article, whatever the sound of the noun.

This follows because the author knows the word better than the sound rule, and an hour is an hour.

#### @spec no-over-several-variables-is-said-as-no-combination

> The verbalizer says `no` over variables of several types as no combination of the variables.

This follows because a statement that none of each variable exists would mean something else than none of them together.

#### @spec a-call-of-a-predicate-gives-its-variables-numbers-that-are-free

> When a called body quantifies a variable that the call already uses, the verbalizer gives it a number that no variable in use has.

This follows because a reader takes two variables with one name for one variable, and the statement would say what the logic does not.

#### @spec a-variable-of-a-body-never-takes-the-name-of-an-argument

> The verbalizer never gives a variable of a called body the name of an argument of the call.

This follows because the argument and the variable would read as one thing.

#### @spec the-alternatives-of-a-list-reuse-a-name-and-keep-it-taken-for-what-follows

> The verbalizer gives the same name to the variable in each alternative of a list, and keeps the name taken for what follows.

This follows because alternatives do not hold together, so one name in each is clear. What follows must not reuse a name an alternative took.

#### @spec the-statements-of-a-list-each-use-the-same-names

> The verbalizer uses the same names in each statement of a list that quantifies a variable of one type.

This follows because statements of a list stand apart, and a reader reads each from its own start.

#### @spec conditions-that-hold-together-keep-their-names-apart

> The verbalizer gives a different name to the variable of each condition in a list of conditions that hold together.

This follows because conditions that hold together may talk about the same thing, and one name would join what the logic keeps apart.

#### @spec a-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-by-its-body

> The verbalizer says a [call](#term-predicate-call) of a predicate with no reading by its body, with each argument in the place it fills.

This follows because the author gave the predicate a body so that it means something, and the body is the next best words.

#### @spec a-negated-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-as-untrue

> The verbalizer says a negated call of a predicate with no reading as "it is not the case that", followed by the body.

This follows because the negative of a body has no words of its own, so the sentence says that the body does not hold.

#### @spec the-reading-of-the-table-wins-over-the-body

> The verbalizer says a call of a predicate that has both a reading and a body with the reading.

This follows because the table is where the author says how a word sounds, and the body is a fallback.

#### @spec the-checker-reads-the-predicates-a-vocabulary-declares

> The verbalizer reads each predicate that a vocabulary declares: its name, what it takes and its body.

This follows because the verbalizer can use only the body of a predicate that has no reading, and the body lives in the vocabulary.

#### @spec a-negation-is-said-with-the-negative-reading-of-what-it-negates

> The verbalizer says the negation of a comparison or a call with the negative reading of what it negates.

This follows because the table gives each word a positive and a negative reading so that no sentence needs a clumsy "not".

#### @spec a-union-on-the-left-is-spelled-out

> The verbalizer says a comparison with a union on its left as one statement for each member of the union.

This follows because a comparison with a union says it of each member, and the reader should not have to unfold it.

#### @spec a-difference-on-the-right-is-spelled-out

> The verbalizer says a comparison with a difference on its right as: the left side is in the first part and not in the second.

This follows because a difference says the right side holds and the removed part does not, which is two statements.

#### @spec a-disj-quantifier-is-said-with-its-variables-different

> The verbalizer says a quantifier with `disj` as the same quantifier with the condition that its variables are different.

This follows because `disj` says that the variables of one declaration stand for different things, and nothing more.

#### @spec a-difference-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition

> The verbalizer says a quantifier over `A - B` as a quantifier over `A`, with the condition that the variable is not in `B`. When `B` is a variable, the condition is that the two are different.

This follows because the variable ranges over the members of `A` that are not in `B`, which is the type and the condition together.

#### @spec a-set-with-no-noun-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition

> The verbalizer says a quantifier over a set `S` with no noun over the signature that holds `S`, with the condition that the variable is in `S`.

Derives from: [`spec-some-or-no-of-a-set-of-things-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-its-signature`](#spec-some-or-no-of-a-set-of-things-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-its-signature)

This follows because each member of `S` is a member of the signature that holds it. The variable ranges over the members of that signature that are in `S`.

#### @spec membership-in-a-navigation-is-said-with-the-reading-of-its-field

> The verbalizer says `x in y.f` and `y in f.x` with the reading of the field `f`, with `y` in its first slot and `x` in its second.

This follows because `x in y.f` holds exactly when `y->x` is in `f`, which is what the reading of the field says.

#### @spec no-or-some-of-a-navigation-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-the-type-of-the-field

> The verbalizer says `no y.f` and `some y.f` as `no` or `some` of the type that the field `f` points at. The reading of the field puts that noun beside `y`.

This follows because `no y.f` holds exactly when nothing is in `y.f`, and the field declares what can be.

#### @spec a-transpose-in-a-navigation-is-said-as-the-navigation-the-other-way

> The verbalizer says `y.~f` as `f.y`, and `~f.y` as `y.f`.

Derives from: [`spec-membership-in-a-navigation-is-said-with-the-reading-of-its-field`](#spec-membership-in-a-navigation-is-said-with-the-reading-of-its-field)

This follows because `~f` holds `x->y` exactly when `f` holds `y->x`. A navigation of `~f` from one side reaches what a navigation of `f` from the other side reaches, and the reading of `f` says that.

#### @spec a-pair-in-a-transpose-is-said-the-other-way-round

> The verbalizer says `x->y in ~r` as `y->x in r`.

This follows because `~r` holds `x->y` exactly when `r` holds `y->x`.

#### @spec some-or-no-of-a-set-of-things-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-its-signature

> The verbalizer says `some S` and `no S`, for a set `S` whose reading takes a variable, as `some` or `no` of the signature that holds `S`. That signature is the one `S` is declared `in` or `extends`, or `S` itself when it stands on its own.

This follows because `some S` holds exactly when a member of that signature is in `S`, and the reading of `S` says what being in `S` is.

##### @spec a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-once-is-said-with-a-noun-phrase-in-its-place

> When the reading of `S` says its variable once, the verbalizer puts a noun phrase of the signature in its place: "an edge is being delivered".

This follows because the phrase names the one member that the reading is about, in the one place the reading says it.

##### @spec a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-twice-is-said-in-full

> When the reading of `S` says its variable more than once, the verbalizer says `some S` and `no S` in full: a quantifier over the signature, with a numbered name.

This follows because a noun phrase in two places would read as two things, where the logic has one.

##### @spec a-set-with-no-one-signature-that-holds-it-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses `some S` and `no S`, for a set `S` whose reading takes a variable, when the vocabulary declares no one signature that holds `S`, and names `S`.

This follows because without the signature the verbalizer has no noun for the members of `S`, and any noun it chose would be invented.

#### @spec a-primed-name-with-no-reading-of-its-own-is-said-at-the-next-moment

> The verbalizer says a clause that primes one set or field as "at the next moment" and the clause without the prime. A reading of the primed name wins.

This follows because a variable is the same thing at every moment. The primed name is then the only part of the clause that the next moment changes.

#### @spec a-set-where-a-variable-belongs-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a formula that puts a set or a field where a reading takes a variable, and names it.

This follows because a reading says something of one thing in each slot. A set in a slot would read as if it were one thing.

#### @spec a-field-of-one-value-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-with-its-reading

> The verbalizer says `x.f = y` and `x.f != y`, for a field `f` that the vocabulary declares `one` or `lone`, with the reading of the field.

This follows because a field of at most one value equals `y` exactly when `y` is in it.

#### @spec a-field-of-many-values-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-member-by-member

> For a field `f` that can hold more than one value, the verbalizer says `x.f = y` member by member. For every member of the type of `f`, it says the reading of `f` "exactly when" the member and `y` are the same. It refuses `x.f != y`.

This follows because a set equals `y` when `y` is in it and nothing else is. The reading of the field says only the first half.

#### @spec two-values-that-are-equal-are-said-member-by-member

> The verbalizer says `y.f = z.g` as "for every" member of the type of `f`, the reading of `f` "exactly when" the reading of `g`. When one side is primed, it says that side "at the next moment" and the other "now".

This follows because two sets are equal exactly when they have the same members. The type of the field holds every member that either side can have.

#### @spec a-rule-of-two-clauses-is-said-on-one-line

<!-- statement-spec-a-rule-of-two-clauses-is-said-on-one-line:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [list_1](#term-series):
>
> when list_1 is a rule whose two sides are each one clause, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 on one line, as "when" the first side, the second side.
<!-- statement-spec-a-rule-of-two-clauses-is-said-on-one-line:end -->

This follows because a short rule is clearest as one sentence, "when this, that".

```alloy
all f: Series | f in OneLineRule implies f in OneLine
```

#### @spec a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-only-where-it-starts-with-its-own-words

> A statement begins with a capital where it begins with its own words, and with the name unchanged where it begins with a name.

This follows because a name from the formula, such as a variable, stays as it is.

#### @spec two-variables-are-said-to-be-different-or-the-same

> The verbalizer says a comparison of two variables as "different" or "the same".

This follows because the logic compares two things, and the reader should hear that they are two, or one.

#### @spec eventually-is-said-as-now-or-at-a-later-moment

> The verbalizer says `eventually` as "now or at a later moment".

This follows because eventually includes the present moment, and "someday" would leave it out.

#### @spec after-is-said-as-at-the-next-moment

> The verbalizer says `after` as "at the next moment".

This follows because after looks one step ahead and no further.

#### @spec until-is-said-as-at-every-moment-before-the-first-moment-where

> The verbalizer says `until` as "at every moment before the first moment where" the second side holds, which comes now or later.

This follows because until holds the first side up to the moment the second side holds, and requires that moment to come.

#### @spec always-is-said-as-now-and-at-every-later-moment

> The verbalizer says `always` as "now and at every later moment".

This follows because always holds from the present on. "At every moment" would also reach back to the moments before it, which historically covers.

#### @spec before-is-said-as-there-is-a-moment-before-and-at-it

> The verbalizer says `before` as `there is a moment before, and at it`.

This follows because before looks one step back, and fails at the first moment, which has no moment before it. "At the moment before" would leave that out.

#### @spec once-is-said-as-now-or-at-an-earlier-moment

> The verbalizer says `once` as "now or at an earlier moment".

This follows because once is eventually turned to the past, and includes the present moment as eventually does.

#### @spec historically-is-said-as-now-and-at-every-earlier-moment

> The verbalizer says `historically` as "now and at every earlier moment".

This follows because historically is always turned to the past, and includes the present moment as always does.

#### @spec since-is-said-as-at-every-moment-after-the-last-moment-where

> The verbalizer says `since` as "at every moment after the last moment where" the second side holds, which came now or earlier.

This follows because since is until turned to the past. It holds the first side from the moment the second side last held up to now, and requires that moment to have come.

#### @spec releases-is-said-as-up-to-and-including-the-first-moment-where-if-one-comes

> The verbalizer says `releases` as "up to and including the first moment where" the first side holds, "if one comes", the second side.

This follows because releases holds the second side up to the moment the first side holds, that moment included. When that moment never comes, it holds the second side for ever.

#### @spec triggered-is-said-as-back-to-and-including-the-last-moment-where-if-there-was-one

> The verbalizer says `triggered` as "back to and including the last moment where" the first side held, "if there was one", the second side.

This follows because triggered is releases turned to the past. It holds the second side back to the moment the first side last held, that moment included. When the first side never held, it holds the second side at every earlier moment.

#### @spec a-sequence-is-said-as-and-at-the-next-moment

> The verbalizer says `a ; b` as "a, and at the next moment, b".

This follows because the semicolon says that the first side holds now and the second side holds at the next moment.

#### @spec a-name-with-no-reading-is-refused-and-named

> The verbalizer refuses a formula with a name that has no reading, and names the word.

This follows because a statement that skips the name says less than the logic holds. The author can mend only what the verbalizer names.

#### @spec a-reading-with-no-negative-form-is-refused-and-named

> The verbalizer refuses a formula that negates a word whose reading has no negative form, and names the word.

This follows because the verbalizer would have to invent a negation, and the invention may mean something else.

#### @spec a-type-with-no-noun-is-refused-and-named

> The verbalizer refuses a formula that quantifies a type with no noun, and names the type.

This follows because a quantifier without a noun for its type cannot say what its variable stands for.

#### @spec a-reading-that-uses-a-slot-the-formula-does-not-give-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a formula whose reading of a word uses a place that the formula does not fill, and names the place.

This follows because the reading talks about something the formula does not mention, and any word put there would be invented.

#### @spec a-reading-that-leaves-out-a-slot-the-formula-gives-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a formula whose reading of a word leaves out a place that the formula fills, and names the place.

This follows because the variable in that place would drop out of the statement, which would then say less than the formula.

#### @spec a-binary-temporal-operator-inside-a-side-of-another-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses `until`, `since`, `releases`, `triggered` or `;` with a side that holds one of them, except a `;` after a `;`.

This follows because the words of each one are a clause with commas, and two of them nested read in more than one way. A chain of `;` reads in order.

#### @spec a-primed-relation-of-a-variable-signature-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a prime on a relation `Sig.rel` that has a reading of its own when `Sig` is a `var sig`.

This follows because the prime then moves the signature to the next moment too. "At the next moment" in front would say that, but the reading of the relation names the signature as it is now.

#### @spec a-construct-the-words-do-not-cover-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a formula with a construct that the words do not cover, and names the construct.

This follows because leaving a construct out would hide part of the logic, and guessing its words could change its meaning.

#### @spec a-line-of-readings-that-cannot-be-read-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a [line](#term-line) of readings that has neither a noun nor a key, and says that it cannot read the line.

This follows because a line the verbalizer misreads would give a word the wrong sentence.

#### @spec a-bracket-with-no-partner-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a line of readings with a bracket that has no partner, and says so.

This follows because a bracket marks the word that links to a term, and half a mark would link the wrong words.

#### @spec a-predicate-whose-body-cannot-be-said-is-refused-with-advice-to-give-it-a-reading

> The verbalizer refuses a call of a predicate with no reading and a body the words do not cover, and advises a reading.

This follows because a body the verbalizer cannot say is no fallback, and the reading is how the author mends it.

#### @spec a-predicate-defined-in-terms-of-itself-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a call of a predicate whose body calls that predicate, and says that it calls itself.

This follows because a body that calls itself never ends in words.

#### @spec a-call-with-the-wrong-number-of-arguments-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a call with the wrong number of arguments, and says how many the predicate takes.

This follows because an argument with no parameter, or a parameter with no argument, has no place in the words.

#### @spec text-that-is-not-a-definition-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses text given as a definition that is not one, and says how to write a definition.

This follows because the verbalizer words a definition as one, and text that only looks like a formula would get the wrong words.

#### @spec a-parameter-with-no-type-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a definition with a parameter that has no type, and says so.

This follows because the statement says "for every" a noun of the type, and a parameter without a type has no noun.

#### @spec a-definition-whose-body-is-a-rule-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a definition whose body is a rule, and says that no words follow "exactly when".

This follows because a definition says exactly when its body holds, and a rule has no words to follow "exactly when".

#### @spec a-definition-of-a-word-with-no-reading-is-refused

> The verbalizer refuses a definition of a word that has no reading, and names the word.

This follows because the statement of a definition says the word it defines, and without a reading it would say nothing.

#### @spec a-passage-that-starts-with-pred-is-a-definition

> The verbalizer reads text that starts with the keyword `pred` as a definition.

This follows because the keyword is how the author says that the text defines a word.

#### @spec a-definition-says-what-it-names-exactly-when-its-body-holds-for-every-parameter

> The verbalizer says a [definition](#term-definition-passage) as "for every" parameter, then the name, "exactly when", and the body.

This follows because a definition fixes the meaning of a word for every value, and "exactly when" says that it holds in both directions.

#### @spec a-definition-that-marks-its-variables-disj-is-said-with-them-different

> The verbalizer says a definition that marks its variables `disj` with the condition that they are different. A call of it said by its body gets the same condition.

This follows because `disj` before the variables of a predicate adds that condition to its body.

#### @spec a-definition-with-a-body-of-one-clause-is-said-on-one-line

> The verbalizer says a definition whose body is one clause on one line after the "for every".

This follows because a short definition is clearest as one sentence.

#### @spec a-definition-says-each-parameter-with-the-noun-of-its-type

> The verbalizer says each parameter of a definition with the noun of its type.

This follows because each parameter is a thing, and the noun tells which kind.

#### @spec a-definition-is-said-in-markdown-the-way-a-formula-is

> In the Markdown layout, the verbalizer says a definition with a blank line between its paragraphs.

This follows because the statement sits in a Markdown document, and a definition in it reads as paragraphs like any other statement.

#### @spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-for-each-kind

<!-- statement-spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-for-each-kind:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage):
>
> when all of these hold:
> - definition_1 is a definition whose alternatives each begin with the kind of the subject
> - definition_1 can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind)
>
> then [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as a list with a noun phrase for each kind, such as "a spec that cites no axiom".
<!-- statement-spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-for-each-kind:end -->

This follows because a reader takes in "a spec that cites no axiom" faster than a sentence about a unit that is a spec. The phrase says the same in fewer words.

```alloy
all f: Definition | (f in GuardedByKind and byKind[f]) implies f in PhrasePerKind
```

#### @spec the-alternatives-of-one-kind-are-put-together-with-or

<!-- statement-spec-the-alternatives-of-one-kind-are-put-together-with-or:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage):
>
> when definition_1 is a definition with two alternatives for one kind and can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as one noun phrase for that kind, with the alternatives joined by or.
<!-- statement-spec-the-alternatives-of-one-kind-are-put-together-with-or:end -->

This follows because two alternatives for one kind are two ways to be that kind, and one phrase says so.

```alloy
all f: Definition | (f in SameKindTwice and byKind[f]) implies f in JoinedWithOr
```

#### @spec the-options-of-an-or-inside-a-kind-are-one-coordination

<!-- statement-spec-the-options-of-an-or-inside-a-kind-are-one-coordination:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage):
>
> when definition_1 is a definition with an or inside one kind and can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says definition_1 as one run of clauses joined by commas and or.
<!-- statement-spec-the-options-of-an-or-inside-a-kind-are-one-coordination:end -->

This follows because options in one kind read as one run of "names, names or is".

```alloy
all f: Definition | (f in OrInsideKind and byKind[f]) implies f in OneCoordination
```

#### @spec a-definition-with-one-kind-is-one-sentence

<!-- statement-spec-a-definition-with-one-kind-is-one-sentence:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [definition_1](#term-definition-passage):
>

#### @spec a-word-that-names-a-term-links-to-the-unit-that-holds-its-reading-in-markdown

> In the Markdown layout, the verbalizer links a word whose reading a unit holds to that unit.

This follows because a reader who meets the word can follow it to what it means.

#### @spec a-word-that-names-a-term-is-plain-in-the-text-layout

> In the text layout, the verbalizer says a word whose reading a unit holds in plain words.

This follows because the text layout has no way to hold a link.

#### @spec only-the-first-mention-of-a-term-links

> In a [linked formula](#term-linked-formula), the verbalizer links only the first mention of a term, in reading order.

This follows because a link on every mention fills the page with blue, and the reader learns the term once.

#### @spec a-word-never-links-to-the-unit-its-sentence-is-in

> The verbalizer never links a word to the unit whose statement it is saying.

This follows because a link to the page the reader is on goes nowhere.

#### @spec a-reading-that-points-at-a-unit-links-to-it

> The verbalizer links a word whose reading points at a unit to that unit.

This follows because the author wrote the link by hand to name exactly where the word leads.

#### @spec a-link-in-a-table-held-in-another-document-goes-through-its-path

> The verbalizer writes a link of a table held in another document, to an anchor of that document, through the path to it.

This follows because a link written as `#anchor` points into the document that holds the table, and a reader meets the words in another.

#### @spec the-nouns-of-a-quantifier-link-and-the-article-follows-the-word

> The verbalizer links the noun of a quantified type whose reading a unit holds, and chooses the article by the word, not the bracket.

This follows because the variable is a thing of the type, so a reader may follow the noun. A bracket must not change a or an.

#### @spec a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-on-the-word-and-not-on-the-bracket

> When a statement begins with a linked word, the verbalizer puts the capital on the first letter of the word, inside the link.

This follows because the capital belongs to the first letter a reader sees.

#### @spec a-reading-held-by-no-unit-has-plain-words

> The verbalizer says a word whose reading no unit holds in plain words, even in the Markdown layout.

This follows because a word with no unit to lead to is only a word.
